utterances.text: I did not say expelled, I said killed and expelled.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: I cannot corroborate that in particular because I was born in 1952 and this has not been recorded in history anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. There are documents about this, but there's no need for me to discuss the matter with you any further. And do you know that the initiative to establish a separate Buzim municipality came into being not in 1995 but the initiative was launched much earlier?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: Well, that's right, because Buzim had the status of municipality all the way up to 1963 within Bosnia-Herzegovina. After this reorganisation, it lost that status, and the local population expressed their wish to have that status returned to them, and this was finally done towards the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So until the 1960s, it was a municipality and then this new organisation took place in the 1960s, and then this larger municipality of Bosanska Krupa was set up and then in 1995 again it became a separate municipality.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: Well, roughly it was that way although the organisation was not after 1963 and then in 1995. The municipality of Bosanska Krupa in 1963 got the status of district or something to that effect. Buzim had the status of municipality in that organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You say on page 4, in paragraph 5 that the Serb Democratic Party of Bosanska Krupa, in 1991, elaborated a study on the administrative division of the municipality, and you say that they justified this by the necessity to establish a separate Serb municipality.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: Not the need to establish a separate Serb municipality, but ultimately to create a united Serb state in the Balkans, as was written in the last sentence quite specifically of that study.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, not municipality but state, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. They said that this was the first step towards the establishment of a unified Serb state in the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Already in the next paragraph you called this initiative of the local Serbs ridiculous because, as you say, this was possible to decide only at the level of the municipality and the republic, by the republican Assembly.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as borders of municipalities wee concerned, according to the regulations that were then in force, it was only the Assembly of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina that could reach decisions to that effect. I don't know if it's a ridiculous term. I wouldn't call it ridiculous. I would call this a very serious signal which indicated what would happen in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, are you aware that Serbs from the area of Bosanska Krupa did not intend for this idea, for this proposal of theirs which, as you say under the legislation was in the competence of the republican and the municipal assemblies, did not intend for this idea to be implemented by passing these organs? They just floated it to you as the SDA in order to reach an agreement, and I suppose it was up to the authorities that you enumerated to vote on it.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: The problem was that they insisted on inter-party negotiations concerning that proposal, and we wanted it to be submitted to the Municipal Assembly of Bosanska Krupa, and they were against it for reasons I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in the municipal assembly, you and the Serbian Democratic Party received -- in fact shared all the deputies between you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: Well, practically that's true, with the exception of five deputies who represented the then-SDP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So your party had the majority in the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, with 64 per cent of MPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So they suggested it to you, the Muslim party, in order to reach an agreement on a joint proposal that would then be submitted to the authorities who were called upon to decide.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: They did not suggest that we submit it to the authorities. They suggested instead that it be a subject of bilateral negotiations between the SDA and the SDS, and we did not want that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask you. Is it true that it was you, yourself, who gave full support to this proposal of the SDS, judging it as completely legitimate and grounded in the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: I never made that statement, but in my eyes, every proposal for a territorial division in Bosnia and Herzegovina was legitimate and legal with the proviso that constitutional and legal procedure was observed. And in this particular case, they were not ready to abide by that procedure. They showed that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said yourself that it was a legitimate proposal and good enough to be discussed according to legal procedure.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. If it was submitted to legal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you do not dispute that it was a legal, legitimate proposal?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember my exact words. It was too long ago. But I believe that I could have said something to that effect, because such an initiative could have legally originated from the SDS. But I want to make this reservation: Not to divide the municipality according to the criteria they suggested but according to various economic and other criteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But is it true that when justifying this proposal to members of your own party, and explaining it, you said it was based on Article 265 of the then constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that this initiative was in keeping with the constitution and that from the viewpoint of legality, it cannot be challenged?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: That initiative was never challenged because nobody was given a chance to challenge it or consider it, because they refused to start a serious discussion before the competent authorities, either in the municipality or in the republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I understand that. But is it true that if we continue with this example of the SDS, you made a similar proposal with relation to Buzim, then the largest municipality within Bosanska Krupa and nowadays a separate municipality?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: As you said yourself, that initiative existed even before and had been submitted to the republican Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, the republican Assembly referred this work, in fact suspended the work on this proposal relating to Buzim and seven other municipalities until the conflict started.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It doesn't really matter whether it was finalised or not. Is it true that representatives of the SDA at one of these inter-party negotiations demanded from the representatives of the SDS to present a feasibility study for the division of the municipality and received that study?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: The proposal for making Buzim a separate municipality was based on specific justified criteria, whereas the Serb proposal was based only on the separation of Muslim and Serb communities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, since this is completely new to me, I understand that this feasibility study was titled "Feasibility study on the social and economic justification of the division of Bosanska Krupa municipality."

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: In our everyday work we just referred to it as "study."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive that study for your consideration from the representatives of the SDS and got a copy that you could discuss?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: We did get a copy, and within the SDS we considered it and found that it was geared at ethnic division of the municipality and was unacceptable to us as such. We were not given a chance to follow the legal administrative procedure in the municipal and republican Assemblies to explain our views.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Velic. Is it true that you gave up considering the idea further due to pressure from the top echelons of the SDS -- SDA because the Muslim community that lived on the left bank of the Una, 9.000 of them, were a minority compared to Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: That is not true. If you check the statistics for the municipality of Bosanska Krupa - and I'm very familiar with it - for the 1990s and later on, you will see that on the left bank of the Una River there were more Muslims than Serbs. So it could not have affected Buzim as a separate municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the left bank of the Una.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: The Muslim population was the majority in both cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It is up to me to ask and up to you to answer.

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: I have answered and I'm absolutely sure of what I'm saying. In both versions, the Muslim population was the majority on both banks of the Una River. On of the left bank in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you supported the idea at the time, tell me, why are you against it now?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: I never said that I supported it, and I did not support it. I said, on the contrary, that the proposal of the SDS was based only on ethnic considerations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, according to what criteria and with what motivation did Buzim become a separate municipality in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: For reasons that existed even during the war. Buzim was a separate entity removed about 30 kilometres from Bosanska Krupa. It was justified for it to become a separate municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did it maybe happen because in 1995, after the signing of the Dayton Accords, there were no Serbs any more in Buzim because they had left the area en masse because most of their territory was given over to the federation?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: As for how and why Serbs left the territory of Bosanska Krupa, I only learned about it from the media. I wasn't there. I was not a witness of these events. However, I do not believe that the reason for the secession, quote unquote, of the Buzim municipality is the one you quoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, on page 3, paragraph 12, you speak about the ethnic structure of the senior staff of the SDA. You say that Mehmed Mahic was on top; chief of police was your own brother, Semsudin Velic; chief of Territorial Defence was first Hasan Sisic then Hasim Djulic. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct information, and this ethnic structure was established after the elections in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the only municipal official who was a Serb at the time was Gojko Klickovic, who was vice-president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ESAD VELIC
utterances.text: That's not correct because even the then-president of the SDS, Miroslav Vjestica, was the secretary of the Secretary for Agriculture; Mirko Orelj was secretary of the Secretariat for Land Management; and the SDS nominated another person for the post of commander of the police in Bosanska Krupa. Those changes were implemented to the full in Bosanska Krupa, and they were based on inter-party agreements that were fully accepted by the SDS on the basis of election results and the ethnic structure of the municipality itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm going to interrupt you now. We've gone beyond our time. We're going to adjourn. You will have 40 minutes cross-examination left on Wednesday. Mr. Velic, could I ask you to be back, please, on Wednesday morning at 9.00 to continue with your evidence. And I must warn you formally, as we must warn all witnesses, not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. Mr. Nice, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I don't know if you received a note that there were just a couple of matters I'd like to raise procedurally before the Court adjourns today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We've got the witness here. Can you deal with them briefly while he's here?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: They don't concern him at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It means taking the blinds down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. They relate to a recent decision that the Chamber has made on our omnibus motion for additional witnesses, and the Chamber will recall making its order on the 30th of September where we were to provide the list, following which we provided the schedule, which is in a sense the list, and the application to have added to the other list of witnesses various named witnesses. May this be in private session, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Shall we allow the witness to go, because he doesn't want to hang about. Mr. Velic, if you'd like to leave. This is something which doesn't concern your evidence at all. If you would just wait a moment while we take the blinds down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 26th day of November, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.58 p.m.,
